blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by a red border only) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Keep the red border but add, under each invalid field, a text message saying what is wrong and how to fix it ("Enter a 5-digit postcode"), associated with the input through `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input while it is invalid. Today a screen reader user who tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing, and on returning to the field hears only its label: nothing tells them it is invalid nor why; a colour-blind user cannot tell the red border from the grey one; and with the top error list removed, there is no text left anywhere. WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Update the spec's scenarios ("the field's border turns red", "the border returns to grey") so that they require the message and `aria-invalid`, and task 1.2 to test them.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by a red border only

findings.evidence: Each field validates on `blur`. An invalid field gets the class
findings.recommendation: The plan removes the error list at the top of the page and only describes validation on `blur`; it does not say what happens on submit when a field is invalid or was never visited. If submit is simply blocked, a keyboard or screen reader user presses Enter on the submit button and nothing is announced. Specify that on a blocked submit every field is validated and focus moves to the first invalid field (whose message is then read through `aria-describedby`), and add a scenario for it. WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order. Confidence low: the current submit handling in `web/src/checkout/Form.tsx` may already do part of this.
findings.title: Nothing says where focus goes when the form is submitted with errors
